rubrics.criterion: The shared library's plugin-presence probe (the one the config fast path consults) no longer re-derives the rustc toolchain label, the afl.rs package label, or the runtime data directory inline; it reaches those facts through the crate's helper layer again.
rubrics.rationale: This is the smallest of the four inlining sites and the one called as part of the tool's reuse fast path; if it still carries its own copy of the labeling and directory knowledge, the duplication the task complains about is unresolved at its most-reused point.

rubrics.criterion: The `config` subcommand implementation derives the toolchain label, the package label, the runtime directory, and the object-file destination through single-owner helper code, with no second inline derivation left in its body.
rubrics.rationale: The config cluster hosts the largest pair of inline label/directory copies; a repair that leaves an inline variant here keeps the crate's directory-layout knowledge forked even if other sites are fixed.

rubrics.criterion: The AFL++ make-based build and the runtime object installation live in named, delegating step code outside the config body — the subcommand orchestrates calls to build/install steps rather than performing the make invocation, its environment, the success check, and the artifact copy inline. Any well-scoped home for those steps counts, including reinstating the pre-existing step functions.
rubrics.rationale: Beyond copying helpers, the config cluster also folded away two whole build steps; genuine resolution requires the orchestration to be step-shaped again, not merely smaller. The equivalence clause ensures a new decomposition is not penalized for guessing differently.

rubrics.criterion: The binary's startup function delegates AFL++ version discovery, command decoration, and the update notice to well-scoped callees instead of carrying inline closures that re-implement them; the startup body only sequences the steps and consumes their results.
rubrics.rationale: The startup cluster absorbed three different sub-implementations in one narrative; unless version discovery, decoration, and noticing are delegated again, the entry point remains a multi-concern monolith regardless of how tidy it looks.

rubrics.criterion: The binary's cargo driver flow obtains the plugin directory, the plugin-presence answer, and the `-Z llvm-plugins` flag string from single-owner code instead of re-deriving labels, creating the directory, scanning it, and accumulating the flags inline next to each gating check.
rubrics.rationale: The driver cluster duplicated the flag-assembly logic whose ordering constraints every downstream fuzzing build depends on; leaving a second accumulation loop there keeps an operationally dangerous copy alive.

rubrics.criterion: The repair was not achieved by deleting or gutting the copied-from helpers or their callers: the helper seams that the shared library, the binary production paths, and the unit tests rely on remain present, and the orchestration paths actually call them.
rubrics.rationale: The natural gaming move for duplicated-body findings is to make the originals disappear so nothing matches them. In this repository two of the helpers have remaining production callers and several are called directly by unit tests, so deletion either breaks the build or shrinks the crate's public helper contract; the criterion accepts any repair that restores delegation instead.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, each of the shared pieces of knowledge — toolchain labeling, package labeling, runtime directory resolution, plugin presence, plugin flag assembly, version discovery, update notice — has exactly one live implementation reachable from every consumer across both crates.
rubrics.rationale: This is the acceptance-level outcome of the whole task rather than of any single site: it fails if the solver fixes three of the four sites or fixes all sites but leaves a divergent fork of one helper behind.

rubrics.criterion: Where a caller needed a different shape than the current helper provides (an `Option`-returning version probe, a decoration closure, pass lists conditioned on flags), the helper layer was adapted or extended — new well-scoped helpers, adjusted signatures, or small wrappers — so callers delegate instead of re-implementing.
rubrics.rationale: The inline copies exist partly because the original helpers return shapes that were awkward at those call sites (Result vs Option, backing data vs side effect). A sound repair must reconcile those shape mismatches in the helper seam; silently keeping an inline copy because 'the helper doesn't fit' is the failure mode this grades.

rubrics.criterion: The binary's uses of the shared library's knowledge were coordinated with the library side: the shared helper layer serves the binary's startup, driver, and config flows through the same seams, with no binary-local duplicate of a shared-library responsibility introduced by the repair.
rubrics.rationale: The duplication spans a crate boundary (the binary re-derives what the shared library owns). Grading needs to catch the plausible half-repair that restores delegation inside each crate but leaves the binary calling a private copy of library knowledge.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not leave any caller depending on a helper that the same patch marks as uncalled or reference-only — annotations and call topology agree everywhere in the touched files.
rubrics.rationale: The pre-existing state pairs restored calls with stale 'not called anymore' prose and dead-code allows; a solver who rewires callers without touching those markers produces a source file that actively misdescribes itself, which is the residual of the original hazard.

rubrics.criterion: Dead-code allowances that existed only because the helpers had been inlined away (the `#[allow(dead_code)]` attributes added by the inline refactor) are removed once the helpers are live delegation targets again.
rubrics.rationale: Those allowances are the artifact most specific to this refactor; leaving them on live code both masks future genuinely-dead code and preserves the hazard's paper trail.

rubrics.criterion: Narrative comments describing the inlined arrangement as current are gone or rewritten: no comment in the touched files claims a helper 'is not called anymore', describes the inline derivation as the settled replacement for 'old indirections', or presents build steps as 'the previous layout kept as a reference'.
rubrics.rationale: The stale prose is designed to make a reader trust the inline arrangement; leaving it next to restored delegation is contradictory and misleads the next maintainer exactly like the original.

rubrics.criterion: No unused locals, closure constants, leftover imports, or now-redundant intermediate bindings introduced by the extraction remain in the touched functions (for example, scaffold bindings that only existed to host pasted-in bodies).
rubrics.rationale: Extraction commonly leaves the scaffolding of the inline arrangement behind (pre-bound values that used to feed copies); these are inert but confuse readers about which facts are live.

rubrics.criterion: User-facing CLI behavior is byte-identical: subcommand dispatch, flags, help and usage text, and every emitted line the user can see (including the update-notice warning and the missing-runtime guidance produced by the startup path) are unchanged in content and trigger conditions.
rubrics.rationale: The recorded suite covers help/dispatch structure but not the dynamic messages (update warning, runtime guidance) introduced recently; a refactor must not silently change wording or the conditions under which the startup path refuses to run.

rubrics.criterion: The on-disk contract is preserved: the xdg data-directory scheme (`<data dir>/afl.rs/<rustc label>/<afl.rs version>/<subdir>`) and the placement of the runtime object file and plugin shared objects are unchanged for a given toolchain.
rubrics.rationale: Runtime artifacts already built by earlier releases must keep resolving: a refactor that alters path assembly order or label composition silently invalidates every installed toolchain directory.

rubrics.criterion: The make-based AFL++ build keeps its process contract exactly: same make invocation and working directory, same environment (skip-legacy-x86 switch, target directory, empty prefix, DEBUG removal, LLVM config only when plugins are requested, build-only mode otherwise), output suppression unless verbose, and failure still reported rather than ignored.
rubrics.rationale: The build step was inlined as a re-idiomatized builder chain; moving it back into step code is the moment an environment detail (a dropped env var, changed working directory, reordered success check) is most likely to be lost, and none of it is exercised by unit tests.

rubrics.criterion: The compiler-driver contract is preserved: the `-Z llvm-plugins` flags come out identical in content and order for every combination of plugin and cmplog settings (dict2file always, cmplog passes when enabled, ijon once when plugins are present, each followed by its directory-qualified path), and the runtime object file is still appended as the final link argument.
rubrics.rationale: The flag assembly was duplicated next to its gating checks; the pass list and its per-pass path qualification are exactly what downstream rust invocations parse, so an extraction that changes ordering or separators breaks real fuzzing builds in ways the recorded suite cannot catch.

rubrics.criterion: The update notice and the version probe stay best-effort: a failed network probe or unparsable response leaves startup proceeding exactly as before, without altering the exit behavior or emitting additional output; error paths keep surfacing as `anyhow` errors from the same operations instead of new panics or process aborts.
rubrics.rationale: While inlining, error styles drifted (`?`, `unwrap`, `let ... else`); behavior is only preserved if failures stay non-fatal where they were and propagated where they were. Converting a fallible helper to an unwrap at a startup boundary would pass the tests yet break a fresh-checkout user.
